items.text: The 'user != null' term in isConditionalPasskeysEnabled reverses the old condition (context.getUser() == null), so on first login the user is unset and fillContextForm no longer runs, breaking passkey login on the start page of both UsernamePasswordForm and UsernameForm

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

In UsernameForm.java line 47, isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called with zero arguments, but the only definition in parent class UsernamePasswordForm requires one UserModel parameter, causing a compilation error
The null-user login path never gets conditional passkey UI populated, so the initial username page drops passkey conditional UI
Test methods webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication and webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication have significant code duplication, with about 60 lines that could be consolidated

isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requires user != null, which means webauthnAuth.fillContextForm() won't run when the username/password form is the first step and no user is identified yet; since the templates render the #webauth form only when enableWebAuthnConditionalUI is set, this could unintentionally disable conditional passkeys on the initial login page
Change enables passkeys during re-authentication (prompt=login) and changes identity-first organization flow but no documentation was updated
shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators overrides WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators without @Override annotation, risking silent failure if parent method is renamed

PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest catches Exception when asserting the webauthn form is absent, so unrelated WebDriver failures (timeouts, driver errors) are treated as expected and can produce false-positive test passes - should catch NoSuchElementException specifically
`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` is invoked without the required `UserModel` argument, causing an unresolved method call
isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called with no arguments but now requires a UserModel parameter, causing a compile error - should pass context.getUser() as the argument

The new user parameter is only null-checked but user credentials are never checked (e.g., credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthn passwordless type)), so during re-authentication a user with no passkey still gets the passkey form
The new `user != null` check disables conditional passkey form setup for normal (unidentified) login, so passkey sign-in only works when a user is already preselected

shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators overrides WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators without @Override annotation - if the parent method is renamed, this override will silently stop applying
Same element absence check issue at lines 312-317 - try/catch pattern should be replaced with Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)

reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test disables passkeys for the whole realm (setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)) instead of testing the scenario where passkeys are enabled but user has no passkey, hiding the missing per-user check

findElement throws NoSuchElementException when element doesn't exist (doesn't return null), and catching generic Exception is too broad - should use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) instead
In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

Element-absent checks at :290-295 and :311-317 use incorrect pattern 'try { assertThat(findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...) } catch (Exception)' - the inner assertion can never pass and only works because AssertionError is not an Exception; should use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) per suite convention

The new predicate 'webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null' inverts the old condition - passkey data was previously filled only when no user was set, but now fillContextForm no longer runs on normal first login, breaking passkey login on the start page
Commit hygiene issues: change is two commits instead of one squashed, second commit missing Signed-off-by trailer and 'Closes #' link, first commit uses lowercase 'closes' and links two issues

Absence checks at ~:289-295 and ~:310-316 use 'try { assertThat(findElement(..), nullValue()); fail(..) } catch (Exception)' where assertThat is dead code; should use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) like rest of suite

UsernameForm.java:47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the method requires a UserModel parameter after commit 3214b18 changed the signature to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user), causing a compilation error. The fix is to call isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) instead.

UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but commit 3214b188de changed the only declaration to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) with no zero-argument overload, causing compilation failure
Typo 'Succesful' should be 'Successful' at line 413

setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError re-implements AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth by parsing the same auth note, creating code duplication and widening USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH from protected to public
The patch adds an unused PasswordCredentialModel import

setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError re-implements auth-note parsing that already exists in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth, creating duplicate code that could drift apart and widening USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH from protected to public

UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only declaration was changed to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) - no zero-argument overload exists, causing compilation failure
Catch `NoSuchElementException` instead of `Exception` so unexpected Selenium/runtime failures do not get treated as successful assertions

UsernamePasswordForm now only enables conditional passkeys UI when context.getUser() is non-null, which prevents enableWebAuthnConditionalUI from being set during normal unauthenticated login, effectively disabling discoverable-passkey login

issues.claim: The new `user != null` term in `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` reverses the old `context.getUser() == null` condition. As a result, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` no longer runs on the initial login page, where no user is set yet. Conditional passkey UI (`enableWebAuthnConditionalUI`) is therefore not set up for unidentified, first-time passkey login in `UsernamePasswordForm` and `UsernameForm`.

`UsernameForm.authenticate` (line 47) calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only declaration in `UsernamePasswordForm` now requires a `UserModel` parameter and has no zero-argument overload, so the call does not compile.
The test methods `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication` and `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` duplicate about 60 lines of code.
The change enables passkeys during re-authentication (`prompt=login`) and changes the identity-first organization flow, but no documentation was updated.

The webauthn-form absence checks in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` (around lines 289-295 and 310-317) use `try { assertThat(findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...) } catch (Exception)`. The inner assertion is dead code because `findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` rather than returning null. Catching the generic `Exception` treats unrelated WebDriver failures as expected.
The new `user` parameter is only null-checked; the user's passkey credentials are never checked. During re-authentication, a user with no passkey is still shown the passkey form.

The `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` test disables passkeys for the whole realm via `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)` instead of testing a user without a passkey while passkeys are enabled.
The change has two unsquashed commits. The second commit lacks a Signed-off-by trailer and a 'Closes #' link. The first commit uses lowercase 'closes' and links two issues.
Line 413 contains the typo 'Succesful' instead of 'Successful'.

`setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` re-implements the auth-note parsing in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth`. It also widens `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` from protected to public.
The patch adds an unused `PasswordCredentialModel` import.
